title: Settlements (built-up areas)
summary: Outlines of every village, town centre and city in Maine, drawn by clustering building footprints. Used at zooms 7-12, where the 925k footprints are too dense to draw.

inputs.name: src_overture.buildings
inputs.role: Building footprints (Overture Maps). One point is taken on each footprint.

inputs.name: src_census.cousub
inputs.role: Towns (county subdivisions): each settlement is named after the town holding most of it.

inputs.name: src_census.county
inputs.role: County name, joined through the town GEOID.

steps.title: One point per building
steps.detail: A point on the surface of each footprint, projected to UTM 19N (EPSG:26919) so distances are in metres. The footprint area is kept for the footprint_acres total.

steps.title: Cluster the points (DBSCAN)
steps.detail: Statewide ST_ClusterDBSCAN: a building joins a cluster when at least 4 buildings lie within 58 m. Buildings with no such neighbours stay unclustered and are not part of any settlement.
steps.math: p \text{ is a core building} \iff \bigl|\{\, q : \lVert p - q \rVert \le \varepsilon \,\}\bigr| \ge k, \quad \varepsilon = 58\ \text{m},\ k = 4

steps.title: Close each cluster into a shape
steps.detail: Buffer the cluster's points out 60 m, then back in 35 m. The outward buffer fills the gaps between houses; the inward one pulls the edge back so it hugs the outermost buildings (about 25 m beyond them).

steps.title: Dissolve touching shapes
steps.detail: Shapes that touch or overlap are merged into one settlement (a second DBSCAN with distance 0). This joins a city split by parking lots and highways wider than the cluster distance.

steps.title: Simplify and filter
steps.detail: Simplified to 5 m (topology preserved). Settlements with fewer than 10 buildings are dropped.

steps.title: Name and classify
steps.detail: Town = the town containing a point on the settlement's surface. Size class from the building count: 1000+ city or large town, 250+ town centre, 50+ village, otherwise hamlet.
steps.math: \text{class}(n) = \begin{cases} \text{City or large town} & n \ge 1000 \\ \text{Town centre} & 250 \le n < 1000 \\ \text{Village} & 50 \le n < 250 \\ \text{Hamlet} & 10 \le n < 50 \end{cases}

parameters.name: Neighbour distance (DBSCAN eps)
parameters.why: Raised from 50 m. Density scales with distance squared, so 58 m admits areas about 25 % less dense.

parameters.name: Minimum neighbours (DBSCAN minpoints)
parameters.why: Keeps a farmhouse with a barn and two sheds from seeding a cluster.

parameters.name: Buffer out / in
parameters.why: Out must exceed half the neighbour distance so neighbours' buffers join; the net 25 m keeps yards inside the outline.

parameters.name: Simplify tolerance
parameters.why: Below a pixel at zoom 12; cuts vertex count for tiles.

parameters.name: Minimum settlement size
parameters.why: Below this the shape is a cluster of outbuildings, not a place.

parameters.name: Size classes
parameters.why: Separates cities, service towns, villages and hamlets.

caveats: Scattered rural houses are not in any settlement by design, so the buildings in settlements are well below the footprint count.
A settlement spanning two towns is named after one of them only.
acres is the outline's area; footprint_acres is the area of the buildings themselves.

Rebuilt only when the number of building footprints changes (about two minutes). An Overture update that keeps the same count is not picked up; to force a rebuild run TRUNCATE src_units.settlements_meta, then ./mapgen apply maine-places.
